decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom is a high-value niche option that is only now being released, so its uncertainty is unresolved and abandoning it before US release would forfeit its upside.
Small volume chambers serve the growing small-field and stereotactic dosimetry market, and keeping one listed in an existing catalogue costs little while its value is still emerging.
This chamber overlaps with Product B, but one year of evidence is too little to tell which variant will win, and keeping both open is cheap.
A standard clinical ionization chamber is a core, low-risk product for a dosimetry manufacturer, with steady demand and negligible holding cost.
A relative dosimetry chamber complements the firm's water phantom systems, so keeping it preserves the value of the product portfolio at little cost.
Thimble chambers are a staple of radiation dosimetry, and nothing in the early results suggests its value will not be realized.
